content:
jordan: Heads up — the mass re-encrypt job for tenant batch-42 is getting repeated ThrottlingExceptions from AWS KMS, progress stalled ~38%. Anyone seen this pattern before?

sam: saw similar last month — usually KMS API limits plus our concurrent grants. How many workers are running?

jordan: 120 workers right now (k8s HPA). Logs show `ThrottlingException: Rate exceeded` and a bunch of 429s from the kms proxy.

maria: that's a lot. AWS KMS has account-wide request limits for GenerateDataKey/Decrypt. We should gate concurrency per-key and add uniform jitter/backoff.

lee: +1. Also check our rewrap workflow: we call KMS per-object to decrypt envelope key then re-encrypt with new CMK. If we batch-decrypt incorrectly we hammer KMS.

kevin: quick numbers: metric kms.requests 38k/min for the job window, baseline 2k/min. Throttle rate spiked after rollout of higher parallelism yesterday.

ashley: are we using grants or direct CMK policy? Grants reduce KMS DescribeKey overhead. But grants don't change GenerateDataKey limits.

infra-bot: Job runner scaled from 40 -> 120 replicas at 2026-03-18T02:14Z due to backlog. Autoscaler rule: queue_length > 500 -> +4 replicas.

jordan: Proposed immediate mitigation: cap workers to 24 for the job, roll workers down, enable per-tenant token bucket with qps=8/key, and resume. Thoughts?

sam: sounds safe. Also add exponential backoff with full jitter on KMS calls and circuit-breaker that pauses workers for a minute on repeated 429s.

maria: we should surface re-encrypt progress in audit logs as well — include old_key_id/new_key_id and rewrap_job_id in each object-level audit entry. That helps postmortem and compliance.

lee: agree. We need idempotency: include a rewrap_version field on object metadata so retries don't duplicate work.

kevin: for long runs we also need to rewrap in chunks and checkpoint progress by shard. Current job keeps state only in-memory, so any pod restart loses progress and requeues whole shard. Bad.

ashley: can we switch to per-shard checkpoints in Postgres + use Cloud Tasks for at-least-once scheduling? Then each task is small (100 objects) and retries honor backoff.

jordan: plan: 1) scale down to 24, 2) flip feature flag to use shard-checkpoints persisted, 3) update worker to use token-bucket per-cmk, 4) add backoff and circuit-breaker. Implement in next 2 hours.

sam: add monitoring: kms_throttles per_cmk, rewrap_failures, avg_rewrap_latency, and create alert: >5% throttles over 5m for a given key -> pause new shards.

ashley: note differences for other clouds: GCP KMS has per-key qps limits too but error is `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`. Azure Key Vault often returns 429 with Retry-After header. Our client libs should honor Retry-After when present.

lee: good call. Add logic: prefer server-provided Retry-After if available, else jittered backoff. Also cap total attempts to 10 and mark object as "needs manual review" after max failures.

maria: RBAC note: we need a short-lived rotation role for the batch with minimal privileges: kms:Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey only on new+old CMKs, and S3/Object read/write. Add audit entries for role assumption (OIDC events).

kevin: on compliance side, ensure re-encrypt operation writes an immutable audit row: {object_id, old_key, new_key, timestamp, actor=rewrap_job_vX}. We'll log to audit cluster with retention 7 years.

jordan: @ashley can you prepare the small runbook snippet for on-call if throttles recur? Put in docs/runbooks/re-encrypt-throttle.md and link in the alert.

ashley: will do. Draft snippet: `If kms_throttles alert fires -> pause shards, reduce parallelism to 8, check CloudWatch for 429 patterns, escalate to security infra if KMS key quotas hit`. Will include exact consoles/queries.

infra-bot: Patch queued: update worker to token-bucket + backoff at commit 1763abc. Deploy staging in 15m.

jordan: After staging tests, we'll run a canary rewrap of tenant batch-99 (2k objects) and watch kms.requests and audit rows. If green, resume rest in controlled windows (3h batches).

sam: postmortem action: add preflight check to estimator that computes expected KMS QPS = objects * 2 calls / job_duration and warns if >80% of account limit.

lee: we should also consider local envelope key caching for short TTLs to reduce KMS calls for repeated decrypts of same envelope key across objects if we rewrap multiple blobs with same envelope. Need to ensure cache invalidation on rotation.

maria: security signoff required: new rotation role + audit changes. @kevin can you file the minimal IAM change PR and include the audit schema?

kevin: filing PR now, PR link: https://internal.redwood/repos/infra/iam/pulls/402. Adding reviewers: maria, jordan, ashley.

jordan: Thanks team. I'll throttle the job now and start the staged rollout. Post updates here.

sre-bot: Incident update: job mass-reencrypt-batch-42 paused by jordan at 2026-03-18T03:01Z. Current progress: 38%. Next check-in 03:30Z.

jordan: update 03:28Z — scaled down to 24, enabled checkpoints, ran canary for 2k objs -> KMS QPS ~2.5k, no throttles. Resuming at 03:40Z with 3h batch windows and per-key qps limit = 8.

sam: great. After full run, let's have a short retro to capture improvements and tune hpa autoscaler to consider KMS limits. :thumbsup:

maria: adding follow-up item: implement cross-cloud backoff honors (Retry-After) and per-cloud error mapping in our kms-client lib.

jordan: closing loop: will open a follow-up tracking ticket with the mitigation checklist and metrics to watch. Thanks everyone.
